record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.original_question: What physical mechanism keeps the Higgs mass-squared m_h² much smaller than the Planck mass-squared m_Pl²? In particular, if the Standard Model is a low-energy effective theory and new high-scale degrees of freedom at a scale Λ_NP couple to the Higgs boson, what avoids or explains the apparently fine-tuned cancellation needed to keep the Higgs mass light: a symmetry-related mechanism such as compositeness or supersymmetry, or a dynamical mechanism such as a relaxion field?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Standard Model of particle physics regarded as a low-energy effective field theory valid below some high cutoff scale Λ_NP, with the Higgs boson having physical mass-squared m_h² (with m_h ≈ 125 GeV) and Planck mass-squared m_Pl² (with m_Pl ≈ 1.22 × 10^19 GeV), so that m_h²/m_Pl² ≈ 10^-34. Assume that at the scale Λ_NP there exist additional degrees of freedom coupling to the Higgs scalar; integrating them out generates radiative corrections to the Higgs mass-squared parameter of order Λ_NP², which, added to the bare parameter μ², must combine to yield the observed m_h² ≪ Λ_NP² ≤ m_Pl².

Identify and characterize a physical mechanism that naturally enforces m_h² ≪ m_Pl² without requiring a fine-tuned cancellation between the bare μ² term and the radiative contributions. The candidate mechanisms to evaluate fall into two broad classes:

(i) Symmetry-based mechanisms, in which a symmetry of the underlying theory protects the Higgs mass — for example, compositeness (the Higgs arises as a pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson of a spontaneously broken global symmetry of a new strongly coupled sector), or supersymmetry (a fermion–boson symmetry under which quadratic divergences in the scalar mass cancel between superpartners).

(ii) Dynamical mechanisms, in which the smallness of m_h² emerges from cosmological evolution — for example, a relaxion scenario in which an axion-like scalar field scans the effective Higgs mass-squared during the early universe and is dynamically stopped at a small value through a backreaction potential.

Determine whether any such mechanism is realized in nature, and identify the experimental signatures (e.g., new particles, modified Higgs couplings, or cosmological relics) that would confirm it.
artifact.status_search_result: The hierarchy / naturalness problem of the Higgs mass remains an open question in particle physics. No new physics at the TeV scale (supersymmetric partners, composite Higgs resonances, or relaxion signatures) has been discovered at the LHC through the most recent runs, and the question of what stabilizes the electroweak scale relative to the Planck scale is still actively debated in the literature.
